scope: NuGet release-readiness decisions in both current shell owners; no SDK/native implementation or package publication.
findings: Existing C54 feed queries already abort unknown HTTP/transport/JSON failures; no repeated fix is claimed.
Prior readiness conflated all completed non-pass freshness outcomes with a missing release, including superseded versions and invalid reports.
Prior Trusted Publishing domain-substring check admitted a lookalike HTTPS host.

baseline_reproduction.method: Extract the exact prior PowerShell source from Git in memory and execute its existing source matcher and readiness decision block with controlled inputs; no copied source files.
baseline_reproduction.boundary: The fail status alone also covers legitimate absence; the new implementation uses complete per-package observations to distinguish it.

changes: Admit the current feed report schema, exact version and IDs, boolean observations, counts, status and step outcome consistently.
Classify current, missing, newer_version or unknown; block an existing superseded version with blocked_remote_newer_version.
Allow Trusted Publishing only for https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json or the existing nuget.org alias; preserve api_key mode for other feeds.
Expose remote_feed_state in readiness output; keep existing package audit, identity and publication requirements.

node.execution: 79 checks in the decision/PowerShell suite, then seven checks in the full Bash integration run.
node.powershell: Windows PowerShell; actual canonical command and child scripts
node.bash: Native Bash and Python 3 in explicitly selected installed OSM-Ubuntu; actual canonical scripts on the mounted canonical source
node.limit: Native Bash integration declares a skip on ordinary Windows without an explicitly selected WSL distribution. Decision checks require PowerShell and Python. No native Rust or packaged Linux .NET consumer was run.

verification.bash_syntax: bash -n passes for the changed canonical script.
verification.coverage: No line-coverage percentage is claimed for PowerShell/Bash. Closest evidence is 35 decision cases per owner, including each added function parameter, and six full-command scenarios per owner.
verification.initial_failures: First focused attempt passed all six full PowerShell cases but failed two harness arms: Windows command-line length and Python string quoting. JSON input moved to stdin and quoting corrected; product assertions were retained.
verification.transport: Loopback fixtures only; all observed requests were GET. Synthetic byte files and synthetic audit records are test inputs, not release evidence.
verification.secrets: The real NuGet key file was not read. Synthetic-key absence from readiness reports was asserted.
verification.cleanup: Every operation-owned fixture/report tree removed through canonical ownership checks; artifacts/tests/nuget-readiness has no remaining child directories.
verification.storage: Logical bytes removed and physical storage recovery were not measured.

hosted_ci.interpretation: Jobs rejected before execution; inspect account/run annotations for operator action. No hosted source-test or release-validation result follows. No unchanged retry or account mutation performed.

remaining: Linux x64/arm64 native and packaged-consumer verification
Source-authority admission with existing blocked installer links unresolved
Eligible publication and public byte readback
